newsitem.title: UK: U.K. shares hit new closing best, eye 4,000 mark.
newsitem.headline: U.K. shares hit new closing best, eye 4,000 mark.

text.p: Leading British shares hit a new record closing high and set another all-time best on Monday as Wall Street strength continued to bolster the London market, dealers said.
But trading was, at best, modest as early activity prompted by Friday's surge in U.S. stocks quickly faded.

The FTSE 100 index of Britain's largest companies ended the session 9.3 points higher at 3,977.2, beating Friday's close of 3,967.9. The index also squeezed to a new intraday high of 3,980.8, 10 points ahead of its previous best of last week.
The psychological 4,000 level looks a probability in the near term, dealers said, despite the scarcity of trading activity.

Half-year results from a number of second-line stocks failed to provide any momentum to trading after the initial mark-up in prices and though Wall Street failed to fall victim to the expected profit-taking it could not provide sufficient impetus to take London forward in the afternoon.

New York's Dow Jones index edged higher on continuing optimism over the outlook for interest rates, helping the FTSE 100 rally back to near its early highs in late afternoon. By London's close the Dow was 27 points higher at near 5,866.

"People came in this morning all fired up for the market to go through 4,000 and it hasn't quite happened. We haven't seen any real follow-through. People are thinking OK, it may go to 4,000 but then what?', which perhaps brought out some profit-taking," said one senior trader.
But relatively high cash levels among institutional investors remains a support, said Kleinwort Benson strategist Philip Isherwood who has a 4,000 year-end target for the FTSE.
"Institutions are still long of cash and short of British equities. As long as that is the case the downside is limited and the pressure is still on the upside," said Isherwood.

"Corporate results have been good...Profits aren't unravelling, profits are still set to grow. The 4,000 forecast looks timid now. 4,200 was our spillover type of level early next year and is probably going to be achieved this year," he said.
Not all strategists are as sanguine, however, with many still cautious about interest rates.
"It's riding for a fall," said Andrew Hartwill, equity strategist at brokerage Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
"We're anticipating a hike from the Fed (Federal Reserve) either this month or November and we're almost certainly at the bottom of the rate cycle here in the UK," Hartwill added.
Political uncertainty in Britain ahead of the general election which must be held before May 1997, is also expected to take the wind out of the London market.
Results later in the week provided some focus to trading, with building materials group RMC rising ahead of Thursday's figures, adding 13-1/2p to 1,195p.
"There were no real big hitters with results today but there haven't really been any disappointments apart from English China Clays," said a trader.
The shares dropped 9p to 217-1/2p as pre-tax profits fell to 5.7 million pounds from 55.3 million pounds the previous year.
